original_question: Fix an integer r ≥ 1. For a compact Abelian group G with Haar measure and central symmetries s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c, determine exactly which groups satisfy ms_r(G) = 1/r^2.
target_in_paper: Problem 7.4 in §7: "Given an integer number r, detect Abelian groups G with ms_r(G) = 1/r^2." In context, G is a compact Abelian topological group with normalized Haar measure, and ms_r(G) is the maximal symmetry number for the family of central symmetries defined immediately above Theorem 7.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's actual target very closely: it asks for an exact classification, fixes r, works with compact Abelian groups and Haar measure, and focuses on central symmetries rather than a broader neighboring problem. The only real issue is that the paper's formulation is more explicit about the measurable-coloring setup, the exact definition of ms_r, the central-vs-extended symmetry distinction, and it implicitly treats r >= 2 rather than the trivial case r = 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
missing_details: The paper's intended range is r >= 2; the open classification problem is stated for positive integers r in the Ramsey-coloring sense, and the substantive results around it all concern nontrivial colorings. ([mathnet.ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=310&what=fullteng))

G should be stated as a compact Abelian topological group equipped with its normalized Haar probability measure, and all color classes and symmetric subsets are meant to be measurable. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))

The paper uses additive notation for Abelian groups: the central symmetries are s_g(x) = 2g - x. Your multiplicative formula s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c is the corresponding multiplicative-language version, but the refined question should make that translation explicit. ([mathnet.ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=310&what=fullteng))

The quantity must be defined: ms_r(G) = ms(G,S;r), where S is the family of central symmetries, and ms(G,S;r) is the infimum over all measurable r-colorings G = A_1 ∪ ... ∪ A_r of max_i ms(A_i), with ms(A_i) equal here to sup_g μ(A_i ∩ (2g - A_i)) because the symmetries are involutions. ([mathnet.ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=310&what=fullteng))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should make clear that it is about the central-symmetry number ms_r(G), not the larger extended/quasi-central quantity ms_r^+(G) or m~s_r(G). The distinction is essential in the surrounding context. ([mathnet.ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=310&what=fullteng))

The nearby results motivating the classification should be kept in mind: Theorem 7.1 gives the universal lower bound 1/r^2 and an infinite-group sufficient condition for equality, Proposition 7.2 explains the lower-bound mechanism, and Theorem 7.3 gives finite-group cases where equality does or does not occur. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
refined_question: Fix an integer r >= 2. Let G be a compact Abelian topological group with normalized Haar measure μ, and let S = {s_g : G -> G, s_g(x) = 2g - x} be the family of central symmetries of G (equivalently, in multiplicative notation, s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c). Define ms_r(G) := ms(G,S;r) to be the infimum, over all measurable r-colorings G = A_1 ∪ ... ∪ A_r, of max_{1 <= i <= r} sup_{g in G} μ(A_i ∩ s_g(A_i)). Characterize exactly those compact Abelian groups G for which ms_r(G) = 1/r^2. ([mathnet.ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=310&what=fullteng))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: for fixed r >= 2, classify the compact Abelian topological groups G for which 1/r^2 is the sharp universal constant with the property that every measurable r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic measurable subset that is symmetric under some central symmetry s_g(x) = 2g - x and has Haar measure at least 1/r^2. ([mathnet.ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=310&what=fullteng))
justification: The nearest official formulation is the survey's Problem 7.4, which is almost exactly your draft once the paper's notation is restored. It is narrower and more faithful than the neighboring question about the extended/quasi-central symmetry number, because your draft explicitly uses central symmetries and asks for equality ms_r(G) = 1/r^2. The surrounding context in §7 is exactly the right one: central and quasi-central symmetries are defined immediately before Theorem 7.1; Theorem 7.1 supplies the basic lower bound and an infinite-group equality criterion; Proposition 7.2 gives the μ(A)^2 lower-bound mechanism; and Theorem 7.3 gives finite-group evidence that motivates the classification problem stated as Problem 7.4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
